extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, regulatory scholars, law students, journalists, and the public interested in federal regulatory policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing a report offering recommendations to improve U.S. federal regulatory review (ten broad principles) and proposing specific revisions to President Clinton's 1993 executive order to guide the next administration. The page highlights key principles and an implementation-oriented line-by-line markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten regulatory review principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The report 'Fixing Regulatory Review' sets out 10 broad review principles intended to improve the regulatory review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles are followed by a line-by-line markup of Clinton's executive order, allowing the reader to see precisely how the report's suggestions could be implemented by the new administration. (The page does not enumerate all ten principles but states the report contains them.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Better coordination among agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory review should include improved coordination among agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the report's 10 principles; the page presents this as a substantive desideratum for making review more effective across government actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory review should be more transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a core principle in the report; transparency is framed as an element of improving the overall regulatory-review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximization of net benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory decisions should aim to maximize net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named explicitly as one of the report's principles; this reflects a cost–benefit orientation to regulatory assessment promoted by the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: More stringent review of deregulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deregulatory actions should undergo more stringent review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report calls for stronger scrutiny of deregulatory proposals as one of its ten principles, indicating that rollback of regulation warrants rigorous analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: End to discounting benefits for future generations
rubrics_metrics.description: The report recommends an end to the practice of discounting a regulation's benefits for future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a specific substantive change in benefit/discounting practice: the report argues benefits to future generations should not be discounted under current review practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-by-line markup of Clinton's 1993 Executive Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concrete, implementation-focused revision of the existing executive order governing regulatory planning and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report includes a detailed, line-by-line markup of President Bill Clinton's 1993 executive order so readers and policymakers can see precisely how suggested changes would be written into the governing directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cost–benefit analysis to protect environment and health
rubrics_metrics.description: The report builds on the approach advocated in the book 'Retaking Rationality: How Cost-Benefit Analysis Can Better Protect the Environment and Our Health,' favoring cost–benefit analysis as a tool for regulatory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states the report is based partly on that book and on recommendations from experts; this signals that rigorous cost–benefit methods and their application to environmental and health regulation are a central methodological principle of the report.
